tier_reason: Upgraded D->C: the cpp11-branch doc 'doc/单机上rest_rpc和brpc性能测试.md' (2019) publishes first-party same-machine echo QPS tables for rest_rpc vs Apache brpc, and states the CPU (i5-9400F), compiler (g++ 8.2.0) and CMake Release build. It is not A because the benchmark code exists only as partial modification snippets inside the doc (the rest_rpc multi-thread client_thread and its 'high-efficiency mode' are not shown, and there is no runnable bench file), explicit flags are not listed, and the comparison is against brpc, not gRPC.

corrections.baseline: brpc (Apache bRPC); gRPC only transitively, via brpc's own benchmark page
corrections.claimed_speedup: Higher QPS than brpc on a same-machine echo test. Single-thread client: 52631 vs 41667 QPS at 1K (~1.26x), ~1.24x at 8K, ~1.26x at 16K, 16949 vs 8982 at 64K (~1.89x). Multi-thread 1K: 200000 vs 103448 at 6 threads (~1.93x), ~1.50x at 10, ~1.19x at 20. Multi-thread 64K: ~1.72x/1.92x/1.69x at 6/10/20 threads (ratios derived from page data). The page says rest_rpc is almost 2x brpc at 64K. The README's 'far exceeds gRPC' is not measured anywhere; it rests on brpc's own benchmark ranking gRPC last.
corrections.workload: Echo RPC with client and server on one bare-metal machine. The client loops sending 1K/8K/16K/64K strings of 'A', and the server echoes them back with no processing. Server threads equal CPU cores; clients ran single-threaded and with 6/10/20 threads. QPS is the average of several runs. This tested the 2019 C++11 rest_rpc (now the cpp11 branch), not the current C++20 master.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: g++ (Ubuntu 8.2.0-1ubuntu2~18.04) 8.2.0; both projects built with cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release (explicit flags not listed)
corrections.hardware: Intel Core i5-9400F @ 2.90GHz (6 cores), 16 GB RAM, Ubuntu 18.04.1, bare metal; client and server on the same machine
corrections.caveats: The only numbers are a 2019 first-party rest_rpc-vs-brpc doc on the cpp11 branch, which tested the old C++11 version. The link to it from master's README is dead (404), because the doc/ folder is gone from master. The current master README links tests/bench.cpp, which only runs rest_rpc's own echo QPS loop (no gRPC/brpc code, no results). No direct gRPC measurement exists anywhere; 'far exceeds gRPC' is transitive, via brpc's docs/cn/benchmark.md. The benchmark code is partial snippets, and the rest_rpc 'high-efficiency mode' used in the multi-thread runs is undefined. Client timing uses duration_cast<seconds>, so elapsed time has whole-second resolution. The rest_rpc single-thread client uses async_call plus future.wait_for per call.

notes: The record's claimed_speedup had no numbers, so numbers_found_on_page is null. The README quote was checked word for word on master, and the rest_rpc-vs-brpc numbers above come from the cpp11-branch doc. If the orchestrator insists on gRPC as the baseline, the tier against gRPC itself stays D. Master's last commit is 2026-06-23; the record's 2026-09-08 came from the feature branch feat/client-seq-multiplexing. Status is still active; MIT license, not a fork, not archived, 2014 stars.
